title: 3 Unstoppable Dow Stocks to Buy Before October Ends
detail:
3 Unstoppable Dow Stocks to Buy Before October Ends
John Ballard, The Motley Fool

AMZN
V

KO

Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO), and Visa (NYSE: V) are three members of the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES: ^DJI) that continue to post solid financial results in 2026. These companies are unstoppable not because their share prices have been steady, but because each one has competitive advantages that can keep the business growing for years. Here's why they look like solid stocks to buy now.

Image source: Getty Images.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

1. Amazon's cloud backlog is growing at triple-digit rates

Amazon is famous for its online store, but most of its revenue comes from cloud computing, advertising, fulfillment services, subscriptions, and hardware devices like Kindle. The stock has returned about 10% so far this year, slightly ahead of the Dow Jones Industrial Average's roughly 9% gain through mid-October, as of Oct. 15, 2026. Investors have worried about the heavy capital spending needed for cloud infrastructure, which is pressuring free cash flow.

But that spending is tied to the growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) cloud services, with Amazon leading the cloud market. On the July 30, 2026 earnings call, CEO Andy Jassy said the cloud backlog stands at $496 billion and is growing in the triple digits year over year. Amazon's total net sales grew 20% year over year in the second quarter, with analysts expecting full-year sales to be up about 15% over 2025.

The long-term cloud contracts included in the backlog provide Amazon with clearer visibility into future revenue. At the Oct. 15 close of about $255, the stock trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 30, based on Wall Street's 2026 consensus earnings estimate, and 24 times next year's. Wall Street expects roughly 21% annual earnings growth over the next several years, according to consensus estimates. This valuation and growth could support market-beating returns over the next five years.

2. Coca-Cola is using digital tools to reach more consumers

Coca-Cola has a large portfolio of brands, including Powerade, Sprite, and Fairlife. The shares have returned about 34% year-to-date through mid-October, well ahead of the Dow Jones Industrial Average. That outperformance still leaves room for more upside as the company begins to leverage AI tools to drive more demand.

title: Amazon (AMZN) Stock Costs $250 a Share. Here's Why I'd Still Buy It.

Amazon (AMZN) Stock Costs $250 a Share. Here's Why I'd Still Buy It.
Selena Maranjian, The Motley Fool

Just about everyone knows of Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN). Per the 2026 Kantar BrandZ Global Top 100 ranking, Amazon was ranked fourth, with a brand value of $1 trillion. (The company's recent market cap was $2.7 trillion.)

It has been quite good to shareholders, averaging annual gains of 22% over the past 15 years. If you bought in at the stock's IPO back in 1997, you'd be up about 283,000%, enough to turn a $10,000 investment into $28 million! Right now, though, one share costs about $250. That might seem steep, but I'd still buy Amazon -- if I didn't already own it. Here's why.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

The key reason for me is that its stock actually seems appealingly valued at recent levels, despite its torrid long-term growth. Its forward-looking price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio was recently 24, for example, well below its five-year average of 39. (Its price-to-sales ratio of 3.6 was a bit above the five-year average of 3, though.)

Here's an important point, too: A stock's absolute value doesn't mean much by itself. There may be two stocks priced at $250 per stub, and they can be wildly different. One may be tied to a company with a market cap of $100 billion, and the other to a $200 million company. One company may be growing briskly, and the other struggling in the face of multiple challenges. One might be generating loads of cash, while the other is mired in debt that it's having trouble paying down.

That's why you need to compare the price to things like earnings, sales, and so on, and to research any portfolio candidate in depth. Research Amazon and you'll see that it encompasses many businesses, including the fast-growing Amazon Web Services (AWS).

Note, too, that if you don't have $250 to invest, a good brokerage may permit you to buy fractional shares of stock.

title: Amazon Soars 5% as Morgan Stanley Names It a Top Pick: AWS Runway “Under-Appreciated”
detail:
Amazon Soars 5% as Morgan Stanley Names It a Top Pick: AWS Runway “Under-Appreciated”
David Beren
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 2:18 PM CDT 3 min read
AMZN
MS
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Amazon Soars 5% as Morgan Stanley Names It a Top Pick: AWS Runway "Under-Appreciated" ©Preis_King from pixabay, Africa images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Amazon shares rose 5% today after Morgan Stanley named the stock a Top Pick and raised its price target to $350 from $335.

Morgan Stanley's margin forecast for AWS is close to what AWS already earns, so the bigger question is whether its growth keeps speeding up.

Analyst Brian Nowak's roughly $16.50 of 2028 earnings per share is about 24% above the analyst consensus of $13.26.

Amazon's third-quarter report on Oct. 29 is the first test, and AWS's growth rate is the number to watch.

Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) shares are up 5% today after Morgan Stanley named the stock a Top Pick before the open, kept its Overweight rating, and raised its price target to $350 from $335.

That's about 40% above Friday's close. Analyst Brian Nowak thinks the market is missing why, writing that Amazon's "growth and profit runway is under-appreciated."

It starts with AWS

The first of Nowak's five catalysts is faster growth at AWS. He now expects AWS revenue to grow 47% in 2027 and 42% in 2028, up from his earlier 41% and 37%. He raised them after NVIDIA (NVDA:NASDAQ) said it expects AWS to buy and deploy about 2 million of its GPUs over those two years.

That's a lot to ask. AWS grew 37% in the second quarter of 2026, its fastest pace in 18 quarters, so Nowak needs that growth to keep speeding up.

If it does, it adds to a top line that analysts already expect to pass $1.1 trillion in 2028…

Amazon.com (AMZN): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023–2028 (TIKR)

The margins look like the easier part. Nowak sees AWS operating margins of 42% in 2027 and 44% in 2028, and AWS is already most of the way there: in the second quarter it earned $16.6 billion of operating income on $42.2 billion of sales, about 39%.

And Amazon as a whole has more than doubled its operating margin, from 5.3% in 2021 to 11.2% in 2025…

Amazon.com (AMZN): operating (EBIT) margin (%), fiscal 2021–2025 (TIKR)
The Street is a quarter short

Those AWS margins get Nowak to about $16.50 of earnings per share in 2028. The consensus is well below that…

Amazon.com (AMZN): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023–2028 (TIKR)

Analysts expect around $13 for 2028, which puts Nowak about 24% above the Street, and that gap is the "under-appreciated" part. His $350 target works out to about 21x his 2028 estimate, while his note had the stock at about 15x before today's jump.

Of course, all those GPUs cost money. Morgan Stanley's own forecast has Amazon's capital spending climbing to $355 billion in 2027 and $365 billion in 2028, from the roughly $220 billion Amazon expects to spend this year.

Oct. 29 is the first test

My take: Nowak's margin forecast is close to what AWS already earns. So if the chips arrive on schedule, there's plenty of upside from here.

stocks market trading wall street equity -Shutterstock

(Updates with market moves at the end of the day, and other changes, if any.)

The Nasdaq Composite rose Monday in a relief rally following last week's technology-led sell-off, as traders prepared for earnings reports from big Wall Street names, including Meta Platforms (META).

The tech-heavy Nasdaq climbed 1.1% to 26,430.89, while the S&P 500 gained 0.4% to settle at 7,690.73. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged down 0.1% to 51,966.03. Most sectors were in the red, led by utilities, while consumer discretionary paced the winners with a 2.7% advance followed by tech's 1.2% gain.

Amazon.com (AMZN) was up 5%, the best performer on the Dow, followed by IBM and chip-making giant Nvidia (NVDA), with Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) also among the index's biggest gainers.

Nvidia said it ran a record-breaking quantum computing simulation on Jupiter, Europe's first exascale supercomputer, allowing researchers to explore and validate magic state cultivation.

Alphabet likely saw "relatively healthy" Google search revenue growth in the third quarter, driven by higher pricing amid solid search volume, Deutsche Bank said Monday.

On the S&P 500, SanDisk (SNDK), Datadog (DDOG) and Marvell Technology (MRVL) were among the biggest gainers.

Ameriprise Financial (AMP) fell 4.1%, among the worst performers on the S&P 500, after BofA Securities downgraded the company's stock to underperform from buy.

Netflix (NFLX) is expected to report quarterly earnings on Tuesday, with Facebook and WhatsApp parent Meta and electric vehicle manufacturer Tesla (TSLA) scheduled to release theirs on Wednesday after market close.

GE Aerospace (GE), Philip Morris International (PM), Thermo Fisher Scientific (TMO), Procter & Gamble (PG) and American Express (AXP) also report this week.

Oppenheimer Asset Management upgraded its S&P 500 full-year earnings outlook, saying the third-quarter reporting season got off to a solid start. The firm continues to expect the index to close 2026 out at 8,100.

"Our expectations are that another better-than expected quarter is in the offing," Oppenheimer Asset Management Chief Investment Strategist John Stoltzfus said in a report Monday. "Given the economic and corporate fundamentals experienced over the course of recent quarters along with watershed innovation that has seen reports of increased adoption of (artificial intelligence) by businesses and consumers, stocks may well have further upside ahead before year-end."

Treasury yields were higher with the 10-year rate up 4.2 basis points at 5.14%, while the two-year rate rose 3.4 basis points to 4.77%.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil advanced 2.1% to $103.56 a barrel in Monday late-afternoon trade, while Brent dropped 0.5% to $109.37.

US President Donald Trump on Friday signed an executive order to waive key sanctions and tariffs on Russia.

Trump had recently lifted sanctions on Russian diesel exports.

Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping and himself next month to discuss a potential deal to end the Ukraine war, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the discussions.

Spot gold fell 0.6% to $4,140.61 per troy ounce, while silver ticked down 0.1% to $57.25 per ounce.

Tech stocks were higher late Monday afternoon, with the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) rising 1.7% and the State Street SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (XSD) climbing 2.6%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor index added 2.4%.

In corporate news, DXC Technology (DXC) shares rose over 5% after Reuters reported that the company is in advanced talks to sell its insurance software and services division to Eldridge Industries for about $2.4 billion.

Apple (AAPL) is expected to unveil its first touch-screen MacBook at an Oct. 28 product event in Los Angeles, Bloomberg reported. Apple shares were down 0.2%.

American Electric Power (AEP) said Monday it has agreed with X-Energy (XE) to explore the development of a proposed 960 megawatt nuclear energy project in Sullivan County, Indiana. The initial project will use 12 Xe-100 small modular reactors of 80 MW each and Amazon (AMZN) intends to purchase power under a long-term contract, covering the facility's costs and operations, the company said. Amazon shares climbed past 5%.

SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk said Monday on X that he plans to give one of his SpaceX shares to every child in the US next year. Musk beneficially owns about 6.42 billion SpaceX shares, including unvested restricted stock and shares issuable upon exercise of stock options, according to an August SEC filing. SpaceX shares rose 1%.
